candidate.answerReason: The two removed trapezoids each have area 4sH/9, while the regular hexagon has area 3sH/2. The remaining area ratio is 11/27.

methods.label: Subtract the two end trapezoids
methods.explanation:
The desired hexagon is what remains after removing the trapezoids next to \(AB\) and \(ED\). Equal spacing gives their heights, so we only need their parallel side lengths.

Let the regular hexagon's side length be \(s>0\), and let the perpendicular distance between \(AB\) and \(ED\) be \(H>0\). Joining the center to the six vertices gives six equilateral triangles. Consequently, the opposite-vertex diagonal \(CF\) has length \(2s\), and it is parallel to and halfway between \(AB\) and \(ED\).

The diagonal \(CF\) divides the original hexagon into two trapezoids, each with bases \(s,2s\) and height \(H/2\). Therefore its total area is
\[
2\cdot\frac{s+2s}{2}\cdot\frac H2
=\frac{3sH}{2}.
\]
The side locations place \(ZW\) above \(CF\) and \(YX\) below it. Since the four given lines are equally spaced, \(ZW\) is \(H/3\) from \(AB\). This is a fraction
\[
\frac{H/3}{H/2}=\frac23
\]
of the distance from \(AB\) to \(CF\). By proportional segments cut by parallel lines, the two straight sides produce the same fraction of the width increase from \(s\) to \(2s\). Hence
\[
ZW=s+\frac23(2s-s)=\frac{5s}{3}.
\]
By the symmetry of the regular hexagon, \(YX=5s/3\) as well.

Each removed trapezoid has bases \(s,5s/3\) and height \(H/3\), so its area is
\[
\frac{s+5s/3}{2}\cdot\frac H3=\frac{4sH}{9}.
\]
The two removed pieces have disjoint interiors, leaving exactly \(WCXYFZ\). Thus the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{\frac{3sH}{2}-2\cdot\frac{4sH}{9}}
{\frac{3sH}{2}}
=\boxed{\frac{11}{27}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{C}\).
